text.p: Gruma SA de CV said Friday Archer Daniels Midland Co has completed its planned investment in Gruma and the two companies have formed a partnership with their U.S. flour milling operations.
The previously announced transaction, which was cleared by the U.S. Justice Deaprtment earlier Friday, strengthens Gruma's capital structure, the company said.

Gruma gains $258 million, with which it will repay debt and increase cash reserves, the company said, noting this will save some $30 million in annual interest and reduce its debt-to-equity ratio to 0.61 from 1.35.
The company said the interest savings is expected to more than offset the 22 percent dilution to Gruma's earnings per share resulting from the issuance of new common stock to ADM.
The transaction also increases the capacity of Gruma's U.S. corn flour operation and creates a new competitive venture in the $1.5 billion Mexican wheat flour market.

With the completion of the transaction, Gruma said, its U.S. subsidiary, Gruma Corp., owns 80 percent of the leading corn flour producer in the United States and has access to ADM's corn handling and transportation network.
The Gruma-managed venture represents about 23 percent of the combined U.S. market for corn flour and milled corn dough, a $660 million market growing about 5 percent annually, Gruma said.
With the divestiture of one of ADM's three corn mills, as required by regulators, the capacity of the U.S. corn flour operation is about 465,000 metric tonnes per year, Gruma said.
